input: Hi! My fiancé and I are getting married on Saturday 19 June 2027 at a château in the Monts d'Or near Lyon, with 120 guests. The fish course, main, cheese and wedding cake are already agreed with our caterer for a five-course classic French menu, so I just need the starter. I'd love the most classic French wedding starter there is, something my grandmother would call a proper wedding meal: festive and a bit luxurious, since it's a once-in-a-lifetime dinner. It should be recognisably French or Lyonnais and no more than €25 per guest. The caterer needs everything by 31 October, so could you choose the starter and finalize the menu with them?

experiences.name: Pâté en Croûte de Volaille Fermière Label Rouge aux Morilles et Pistaches
experiences.description: Lyon's signature charcuterie entrée, and an elegant, celebratory slice: the city even hosts the world pâté-en-croûte championship. Golden pastry around farm chicken, morels and pistachios, served cold with mesclun salad. Filling of slow-growing Label Rouge free-range (plein air) chicken; made without a foie gras insert, with no force-fed (gavage) product used. Baked as whole pâtés two days ahead with aspic set overnight, then sliced and plated on site; mesclun from a Rhône valley market garden.

experiences.name: Terrine de Foie Gras de Canard, Chutney de Figues & Brioche Toastée
experiences.description: The quintessential French celebration entrée, served at family weddings for generations. A slice of terrine de foie gras de canard per guest, with fig chutney and toasted brioche, plated cold. The duck livers are enlarged by gavage: maize is force-fed through a feeding tube twice daily over the final ~2 weeks of rearing. Livers sourced from Gers (South-West France) producers; terrine prepared 48 h ahead in Maison Tavernier's Villeurbanne kitchen and delivered in refrigerated vans.

experiences.name: Velouté de Châtaigne et Cèpes, Croûtons à l'Huile d'Olive
experiences.description: A comforting velouté of Ardèche chestnuts and ceps, finished with crisp olive-oil croutons. Made with vegetable stock and olive oil, with no cream or butter. Transported hot in insulated containers and ladled into warmed bowls at the château.

experiences.name: Gâteau de Foies Blonds de Volaille Label Rouge, Sauce aux Morilles
experiences.description: A treasured Lyonnais feast-day classic, long served at regional weddings and Sunday banquets. Warm gâteau de foies blonds, a delicate chicken-liver soufflé-terrine, with a rich morel sauce. Made with livers of slow-growing Label Rouge free-range (plein air) chickens; no force-fed (gavage) liver is used, and eggs come from free-range (plein air) hens. Baked in individual ramekins on the morning of the event with morels from a Jura forager cooperative, then finished in the château oven.

experiences.name: Salade de Lentilles Vertes du Puy AOP, Échalotes et Moutarde de Dijon
experiences.description: A bistro favourite: Puy AOP green lentils from Haute-Loire tossed with shallots and a sharp vinaigrette of rapeseed oil and Dijon mustard. Simple and hearty, plated cold, and an easy make-ahead entrée for long tables.

experiences.name: Escalope de Foie Gras d'Oie Poêlée, Réduction au Porto, Pommes Caramélisées
experiences.description: An opulent hot entrée in the grand French festive tradition. Pan-seared escalope de foie gras d'oie with a port reduction and caramelised apples, a luxurious centrepiece for a celebration dinner. The goose livers are enlarged by gavage: maize is force-fed through a feeding tube over the final ~2–3 weeks of rearing. Goose foie gras from Alsace suppliers; seared to order on site by two Maison Tavernier cooks using the château's kitchen.

experiences.name: Tarte Fine aux Tomates Anciennes et Pistou, Roquette
experiences.description: A light Provençal summer entrée: crisp olive-oil shortcrust layered with heirloom tomatoes from a Drôme grower, drizzled with pistou of basil, garlic and olive oil, and served with rocket. Prepared without cheese and baked on site so the pastry stays crisp for every table.
